aria: Animated recap of the Trail Blazers' 118 to 108 home win over Oklahoma City: Damian Lillard's floater with 2:02 left that made it 108-100, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Deni Avdija's 28 points, the top scorers, how the Blazers won, and Friday's game at Sacramento.
notes: Box score from the Portland Trail Blazers' 118–108 home win over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Nov 11, 2026, from the CBS Sports box score and play-by-play, with game details from the AP (Erik García Gundersen, via ABC News, WRAL and FOX Sports), Field Level Media (via GMA News), OKC Thunder Wire (Clemente Almanza, via Yahoo Sports) and VAVEL. All 118 Portland points and all 108 Oklahoma City points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals (56–50 Portland at the half and 88–85 after three, matching Field Level Media). Bench points (34–22) are worked out from the box score's starters; Avdija's 4 steals are from Field Level Media. Rebounds include team rebounds. Records and the Blazers' standing are from the site's standings.

Biggest leads: Oklahoma City's 9, at 23–14 in the first quarter, and Portland's 12, at 64–52 early in the third (CBS play-by-play; the AP says Portland trailed by as many as nine and Oklahoma City by 12). Portland closed the first half on a 15–4 run (AP), took the lead for good at 101–99 with 3:56 left (CBS play-by-play) and made all 14 of its fourth-quarter free throws (Field Level Media). Avdija's 12 first-half points are from Field Level Media. Portland had lost 19 of 20 to Oklahoma City before this two-game sweep (Field Level Media). Isaiah Hartenstein's 20 points were a season best (Field Level Media).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Damian Lillard's floater in the lane with 2:02 left, which made it 108–100 after Deni Avdija's step-back three (AP, Field Level Media, CBS play-by-play). It is drawn as the template's pull-up, not the floater itself. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Portland Trail Blazers or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Lillard’s listed 6-foot-2 and 200 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with arms scaled to his 6-foot-7.75 wingspan at the 2012 draft combine (NBADraft.net), in the Blazers' home white with No. 0 (Basketball-Reference) and his proposed look. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
